security_audit.summary: The audit confirms critical risk from repeated remote installer commands that pipe fetched content into a shell. Most placeholder API key, documentation link, and benign path examples are false positives, but the skill also documents local file uploads and Twitter or X account actions that need explicit user control.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands pipe downloaded content directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell setup with a pinned manual installer flow that verifies checksums and signatures before execution.

remediation.issue: Manual install instructions use command substitution and install a downloaded binary into PATH.
remediation.suggestion: Use a fixed release URL, a structured manifest parser, pinned versions, and verified hashes before moving binaries into executable paths.

remediation.issue: The skill documents automatic upload of local file paths to remote apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for every local file upload and show the exact file paths before running belt commands.

remediation.issue: The skill includes Twitter or X posting and account-action workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval for every post, media upload, direct message, follow, like, or retweet action.

remediation.issue: API key setup is documented through environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secret managers or scoped CI secrets, and warn users not to paste real keys into shared logs or shell history.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with Inference CLI
content.value_statement: Teams often need several hosted AI models, but switching APIs slows routine work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through belt CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains setup and authentication for the belt CLI.
Discovers public and user apps with store, search, category, and detail commands.
Runs inference.sh apps with inline input, saved input files, and version pins.
Handles local file inputs for apps that accept uploads.
Tracks long-running tasks and retrieves saved results.
Lists related skills for images, video, LLMs, search, avatars, and Twitter automation.
limitations: Requires a working belt CLI installation and an inference.sh account.
Remote app behavior, pricing, availability, and outputs are controlled by inference.sh providers.
Local file uploads can expose sensitive data if paths are selected incorrectly.
Account-changing actions require user approval and valid credentials.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multimodal Workflows
use_cases.description: Discover image, video, audio, search, and LLM apps, then compare inputs and outputs from one CLI flow.

use_cases.title: Automate Media Generation Tasks
use_cases.description: Run hosted image, video, upscaling, avatar, and utility apps without managing local GPU infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Run Research Jobs from an Agent
use_cases.description: Use search and LLM apps from an agent session, then track task status and retrieve result links.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to search the inference.sh app store for image generation apps. Show three options and the required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to prepare a small text-to-image job with my prompt. Ask before submitting the remote job.

prompt_templates.title: Track a Long Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to submit a video generation job without waiting. Then show status checks and result retrieval steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multistep Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to discover apps, generate sample inputs, run an image-to-video workflow, and summarize every remote action before execution.

output_examples.input: Search for fast video generation apps.
output: Three matching apps are listed with provider, category, and expected prompt fields.
The response recommends one app for speed and one app for quality.
No job is submitted until the user approves a specific app.

output_examples.input: Run an image upscaling job with my approved file.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the exact file path, submits the selected app, reports the task identifier, and returns the result link when ready.

output_examples.input: Create a research summary using search and an LLM.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects search and language apps, asks before remote execution, then summarizes sources and generated findings.

best_practices: Ask for explicit approval before installing CLIs, uploading files, or posting to external services.
Generate sample inputs before running unfamiliar apps.
Pin app versions for repeatable workflows when available.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers into a shell in unattended workflows.
Do not upload broad directories or sensitive local files as app inputs.
Do not use social media actions without user-reviewed text and account confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires inference.sh authentication through belt login or an API key.

faq.question: Can it run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It sends requests to cloud apps through inference.sh. Local GPU hardware is not required.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can upload file paths passed as inputs. Review paths before running.

faq.question: Can it post to Twitter or X?
faq.answer: The skill documents X automation apps. Use them only with explicit approval and valid credentials.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I check before running commands?
faq.answer: Confirm the app name, input schema, costs, credentials, file paths, and account-changing actions.
